messages:
Maya: FYI team — looks like there's a public report for a driver/kernel vuln impacting NVIDIA Linux drivers (reports referencing CVE-2025-1187). Affects 535.x and older installers when combined with certain kernel configs. Filing triage now.

Jun: Can you paste the advisory link and a short severity note? we need to decide priority for Dedicated clusters.

Maya: https://security.example/reports/CVE-2025-1187 (internal copy attached in ticket). Initial severity: HIGH (local privilege escalation via out-of-bounds in kernel module). Exploits require local code execution but we treat as high for our dedicated and private fleets.

Marco: Quick question — which component exactly? driver userland, kernel module, or CUDA libs?

Maya: Kernel module (nvidia.ko) is the root; installer bundles affected. CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL userland largely unaffected for remote attacks, but compatibility + ABI checks needed when we bump drivers.

InfraBot: (automated) Created ticket INFRA-4821: "CVE-2025-1187 - NVIDIA kernel module triage" assigned to @Maya, severity P1.

Priya: For prioritization: Hosted API (hosted-redwood) can be mitigated by restricting build nodes and container hardening. Dedicated reserved clusters and Private installs should be prioritized because customers run arbitrary workloads. Recommendation: Dedicated/Private = ASAP patch; Hosted = staged after compatibility smoke.

Evan: Agreed. Proposed plan: 1) Build validation matrix (driver -> CUDA -> cuDNN -> NCCL -> PyTorch/TensorFlow), 2) Canary upgrade on two Dedicated pools (gpu-pool-canary-1, gpu-pool-canary-2) with smoke tests, 3) Gradual rollout with monitoring and quick rollback.

Jun: I can own the validation matrix. Any quick commands to identify impacted hosts?

Maya: Commands: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` and `modinfo nvidia | grep version` also check package hashes: `sha256sum /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/video/nvidia.ko` Compare to vendor advisory.

Marco: What about KMS / signing? For Private installs customers might pull vendor packages. Should we require signed driver packages and verify via KMS signature before install?

Priya: We should add a post-install audit log event and verify package signatures for Private. For Dedicated (managed) we can push signed packages from our repo; integrate with KMS (customer-managed keys for Private) so they can assert provenance.

Evan: Also add RBAC change: only infra-admins and sec-oncall can approve driver rollouts. Add audit logging of approval events (timestamp, approver, target cluster).

Jun: Matrix notes — initial compat targets to test: Driver 537.x (patched), CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.1, NCCL 2.18, PyTorch 2.2 wheel + TF 2.12. Test suites: small perf baseline, model load smoke (Llama-like truncated prompt), multi-GPU NCCL allreduce perf, and kernel oops monitoring.

Maya: Good. Also include GPU stress + long-running mkldnn-like batch test for 6 hours on canary. If anything fails, auto-roll back to previous driver (we have image snapshots).

InfraBot: (automated) Added CI job: `ci/gpu/driver-compat-check` to run matrix on canaries.

Priya: Timeline proposal: start canary Monday EOD (UTC), monitor 48h, then phased rollout over 7 days. Notify customers with dedicated infra 24h before their pool is scheduled.

Maya: Owners: Jun = compatibility matrix + CI artifacts, Marco = smoke tests and rollback automation, Priya = customer comms & private-policy KMS signing, Evan = rollout orchestration and RBAC changes. I'll coordinate with sec-oncall during the canary.

Jun: One more: we should add an automated detection alert rule for abnormal kernel module reloads and unexpected modprobe events — forward to sec-oncall and infra pager.

Maya: Agreed. Add audit log entry pattern: `modprobe nvidia` + process owner + container id. Priya please confirm audit retention (we need 90 days for compliance).

Priya: Confirmed — we'll keep 90 days for security-critical audit events.

Marco: Will run an internal compatibility pass today and post initial pass results in INFRA-4821.

Evan: If canary looks good, rollout window next Thu. I'll prepare runbook for emergency rollback (includes commands and snapshot IDs).

Maya: Thanks team — let's keep discussion in this thread for updates. Marking P1. :lock: :gear:
